To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a directional brachytherapy source can be used to treat a curved surface.
a directional brachytherapy applicator is capable of delivering a dose of 100 Gy to the tumor margin while sparing normal tissues.
a directional palladium brachytherapy (DPB) device was developed to deliver brachytherapy in the form of a single, continuous, high‐dose rate (HDR) treatment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the application of the directional Pd‐103 brachrytherapy device on a cylindrical surface and the determination of the dose distribution.
the application of the directional palladium‐ 103 brachytheraphy device to the treatment of the prostate gland.
the application of a directional brachytherapy (BT) device on curved surfaces.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the results of the study are consistent with the hypothesis that the use of a directional Pd‐103 device in the treatment of a large, irregularly shaped, superficial, malignant tumor is feasible and effective.

there is no evidence to support a causal relationship between the use of mobile phones and any adverse health effects, and that no adverse short‐ or long‐term health effects have been established as being caused by exposure to radiofrequency electromagnetic fields from mobile phone use.
the application of the palladium‐103 device on a curved, irregular surface is a feasible procedure that can be performed in a relatively short period of time with minimal complications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated that a directional brachytherapy source, the PDR-103, can be applied to a curved surface with a high level of reproducibility.
we have developed a new device for the delivery of brachytherapy on curved surfaces.
the palladium‐103 directional brachytherapy applicator (PDDA) is an effective device for the palliative treatment of recurrent and/or metastatic disease in the head and neck region.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have demonstrated a novel method for delivering brachytherapy in the context of a curved surface using a directional brachytherapy source, the Palladio device.
we were able to show the feasibility of a directional brachytherapy source in a curved surface phantom.

we have shown that the use of a directional source can reduce dose to the rectal wall, and thus reduce the risk of rectal complications in patients undergoing prostate brachytherapy with I‐125 or Pd‐103 sources.
